description:
Somos Orbita chalaca, un equipo comprometido y proactivo trabajando en el reto Flame in Freefall.

Nuestro objetivo es crear un dashboard inteligente impulsado por IA que resuma, ordene e interprete décadas de experimentos de combustión en microgravedad de NASA, para entregar insights claros de seguridad contra incendios en misiones espaciales.
summary:
Ignis turns NASA's fire-in-orbit experiments into something anyone can explore and play, so future Moon crews stay safe.

Fire behaves differently in orbit: without gravity a small flame turns into a slow, round ball, and some materials keep burning at lower oxygen than in ground tests. Cabins on the Moon and on the way to Mars will likely use more oxygen at lower pressure, and in NASA's PSI records no solid material has been burned in air like that. The answers that do exist are spread over 24 NASA investigations: reports, tables, sensor files and scanned test sheets.

Ignis turns that archive into a pixel-art game anyone can use. Summarize explains each investigation in plain words, with its 72 key findings, every test and NASA's own videos. Rank orders the investigations by how much they tell us about a mission's fire safety, and shows the gap where NASA PSI has no tests recorded. Interpret turns researchers' key messages into what they mean for a crew. A ship simulator lets you set the cabin air and a material and compares it with NASA's real tests, and Sparky, an SI assistant, answers questions using only tool results, always with the NASA source.

Numbers link back to the NASA file they come from, and where NASA's tables contradict the raw data or the reports, our corrections are visible.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Ignis is a web app that summarizes, ranks and interprets NASA's 24 combustion investigations in the Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) archive for spacecraft fire safety. It is built as a 2D pixel-art game so that students, astronauts-to-be and engineers can all use it. Each visitor picks a level (Student, Astronaut or Engineer), and the games and the assistant adapt how much they explain.

- Home: the problem in numbers and three things people believe about fire that orbit proved wrong.

- Dashboard: 1 Summarize (each investigation in plain words, its key findings with sources, every test record, sensor traces, NASA's videos and documents, and where each investigation ran), 2 Rank (investigations ranked for a mission such as the ISS, a Moon base or a Mars ship, with the gap where NASA PSI has no tests recorded), 3 Interpret (what the researchers' key messages mean for a crew), 4 Models (small models fitted to NASA's test tables, with their limits), and Sparky's exam, a quiz graded only against NASA data.

- Simulator: choose a mission, the cabin's oxygen, pressure and airflow, and a material. The ship compares your cabin with the real NASA tests of that material and applies only the rule NASA published (BASS-II Summary Report, Eq. 6.1, for acrylic rods), inside its tested range. Outside the tests recorded in NASA PSI, it says so instead of guessing.

- Relations map: one ball for each material NASA burned in orbit, sized by its number of tests, with how those fires ended.

- Sparky, the SI assistant: answers questions in English or Spanish, by text or voice, using only the data tools, and cites the NASA investigation and file behind each fact.

- The same data tools (14 read-only tools) are published over MCP, so researchers can use them from their own SI assistants.

HOW IT WORKS

A data server built by our team turns NASA's PSI files (reports, data tables, sensor recordings and scanned test sheets) into one table of 2,177 rows (2,059 single tests) and 12 read-only functions. Where NASA's tables contradict their raw files or reports, the correction is a visible patch and the original value is kept. Our backend (FastAPI) is the only gateway to those tools. A worker runs Sparky with LangGraph and Gemini on Vertex AI; the model only proposes, and code validates every answer and page action against fixed schemas before the user sees it. About 23,800 passages of NASA documents are indexed in Weaviate for search by meaning.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Ignis makes space data accessible: designers of lunar and Martian habitats can see in minutes what NASA tested, where NASA PSI has no tests recorded, and how far the closest real test is. Students learn why fire is different in orbit by playing with real data. Claims can be checked back to the NASA source.

On Earth, this research already matters. NASA says microgravity combustion research has led to fire-safety uses on Earth, such as a new type of extinguisher. SAME and SAME-R measured spacecraft smoke so detectors can catch a fire early, and BASS showed that NASA's ground flammability test (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1) is not conservative, because materials burned at lower oxygen in microgravity.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

Science and play together: a pixel-art spacecraft where you light real NASA fire tests, a mascot made of microgravity flame, and a quiz that is graded only against NASA's measurements, never against our own rules.

TOOLS

React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Motion; Python, FastAPI, Redis, LangGraph, Gemini on Vertex AI, Weaviate, FastMCP; Kokoro-82M for Sparky's voice; Google Cloud Run and Compute Engine.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

A valid use of science and the scientific method: never show a number NASA did not measure; say "not recorded" or "no tests recorded in NASA PSI" instead. Keep every source visible. Mark every SI-generated image, text and sound.
